subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: Should a Slack DM be permitted to recall the same agent’s outbound channel activity, and what opt-in scope, retention, redaction, and deletion semantics must constrain that access?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally crosses session-isolation boundaries, so source inspection alone cannot choose the acceptable privacy model or whether a broad existing visibility mode is acceptable.

options.title: Approve narrow opt-in activity recall
options.body: Add a Slack-account/workspace-scoped record of the agent’s own outbound messages and make it available only through an explicitly authorized DM recall path.

options.title: Use broad same-agent visibility
options.body: Allow existing same-agent sibling-session access for this use case, accepting that it reveals more session history than only self-authored activity.

options.title: Preserve isolation
options.body: Keep DM and channel activity isolated unless a future product design establishes a narrower cross-session contract.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow opt-in activity recall
recommendation.body: Add a Slack-account/workspace-scoped record of the agent’s own outbound messages and make it available only through an explicitly authorized DM recall path.
